summary: Good news if you live in San Antonio: we checked, and San Antonio is no stricter than Texas. San Antonio's animal code (ch. 5) prohibits a specific list of wild and dangerous species, such as monkeys and other primates, wolf hybrids, coyotes, foxes, exotic cats, bears, skunks, raccoons, pot-bellied pigs, and poisonous animals. Rats are not on that list, and the code sets no restriction on keeping a pet rat. A pet roof rat is allowed, the same as Texas.

keep.why: San Antonio City Code ch. 5 prohibits keeping a defined list of wild/dangerous species (primates, wolf hybrids, foxes, exotic cats, bears, skunks, raccoons, pot-bellied pigs, poisonous animals). Rats are not on that list, and no separate rule restricts pet rodents. Not stricter than Texas. Confidence medium pending a full read of the prohibited-species section, but rats are absent from the published list.
